About.heading: About us
About.p1: Dsign Accounting is an accounting firm committed to professional accounting and tax services, serving Thai businesses for over 10 years.
About.p2: Our team includes experienced Certified Public Accountants (CPA) and licensed bookkeepers (CPD), ready to advise and support every client need.
About.p3: We believe that good accounting is the foundation of a business that grows sustainably — leave the numbers to us.

q1.q: How is the accounting fee calculated?
q1.a: It depends on the size of your business and document volume. Pricing starts at THB 2,500 per month. Contact us for an actual quote.

q2.q: When does a new company need to start bookkeeping?
q2.a: Bookkeeping must start from the date of company registration, and tax returns must be filed per Revenue Department deadlines.

q3.q: What is VAT and when must I register?
q3.a: VAT is a 7% value-added tax. Companies with annual revenue over THB 1.8 million must register for VAT within 30 days.

q4.a: A tax the payer must withhold and remit to the Revenue Department — for services, rent, advertising, etc., typically 1–5%.

q5.q: How do I send documents to your office?
q5.a: Paper, digital files, LINE, email, or via our upcoming web application.

q6.q: How long does annual closing take?
q6.a: Typically 30–45 days after all documents are received, depending on business complexity.

q7.q: What if I'm audited by the Revenue Department?
q7.a: Our team supports you fully — preparing documents, clarifying records, and negotiating with officials.

q8.a: We serve all of Thailand via online tools, with on-site teams in Bangkok and surroundings.

finish.titleAssessment: Should you incorporate? — for your case

likely.label: Incorporating likely fits you
likely.headline: Several strong reasons line up in your case
likely.body: From the reasons you gave, a company fits how you work. We can register it and set up the accounting end-to-end — and we always confirm everything with you before anything is filed.

considering.label: Worth considering
considering.headline: Real upsides and real trade-offs — weigh both before deciding
considering.body: There's a real case for it, and a real recurring cost. Talk to us and we'll walk through your exact situation — free.

numbers.label: Let's run your numbers
numbers.headline: Your answer points at the tax math — that deserves a real calculation, not a guess
numbers.body: Whether a company saves you tax depends on your actual profit and expenses. Talk to us and we'll compute it both ways with you — free.

none.label: No strong reason stood out yet
none.headline: Many businesses don't need to rush this
none.body: From what you told us, staying as you are looks reasonable for now. We'll tell you the moment that changes — and you can re-check anytime.

foreign.label: You'll likely operate as a Thai company
foreign.headline: Here's the yearly accounting cost once it's running
foreign.body: Foreign owners typically operate through a Thai company. Your setup — ownership structure, capital, work permits — is quoted case-by-case after a free consult; the recurring cost below applies once you're running.

juristic.label: You’re already a company
juristic.headline: Focus on clean books and on-time filing
juristic.body: As a company, what matters now is complete books, year-end statements and filing on time. We can run all of it — your yearly cost is below.

finish.prosEmpty: No strong reason stood out from your answers — which is fine; many businesses needn’t rush.

pros.corpClients: Company clients want tax invoices and withhold tax — as a juristic entity you can take that work and issue exactly the documents they need.
pros.corpCustomers: Most of your customers are already companies — one of the strongest practical reasons to incorporate.
pros.credibility: More credibility — easier with banks, tenders and long-term contracts with organisations.
pros.liability: Limited liability — if the business owes money, your personal assets are protected (you risk only unpaid share capital).
pros.funding: Ready to borrow, take partners or sell shares / raise capital — banks and investors need a juristic entity.
pros.hiring: Supports hiring — proper payroll and social security (5% each side, max ฿750/mo).
pros.smeRates: SME corporate rates are tiered — first ฿300,000 exempt, then 15% up to ฿3M — versus personal rates up to 35%. Worth running your real numbers.

cons.cost: A recurring cost (from ≈฿46,000/yr at Dsign) and a legally-required annual audit — even in years with no profit.
cons.discipline: You must keep formal books and file every month — more documents and discipline.
cons.dividends: Money in the company isn’t personal money — take it out via salary (a deductible cost) or dividends (10% withholding). It needs planning.

cost.titleIf: Estimated yearly cost if you incorporate
cost.setupNote: Incl. government fees + VAT / employer registration when needed
cost.auditNote: Required by law for every company, even loss years
cost.foreignSetupNote: Your setup (ownership structure, capital, work permits) is quoted case-by-case — after a free consult.
cost.counterIndividual: As an individual your accounting cost is very low (~฿5,000–30,000/yr), you file once a year, and at lower profit the 60% deemed-expense deduction can leave you paying less tax than a company would.
cost.counterForeign: From 1 Jan 2026, nominee rules tightened — Thai shareholders in foreign-linked companies must show 3 months of bank statements proving real capital. Foreign-owner setup (FBA/BOI, registered capital, work permits) is quoted case-by-case.
cost.counterScale: These are starting prices for a small, low-volume company; they grow with documents and staff (a fully active company often runs ฿80,000–200,000+/yr). We quote clearly up front — no hidden fees.
